nodes.label: Iron Rule
nodes.rationale: A wrong fast number is worthless. An implementation whose GradeBot error exceeds ERR_TOLERANCE is never benchmarked, never tuned, and its numbers are never recorded, so correctness gates every rung.

nodes.label: GradeBot Harness
nodes.rationale: Allocates a 256MiB input pool, 8 reps at N=2048 with the first discarded as warm-up, a different A each rep, and ping-pongs the C buffer, so cross-rep result caching is defeated by design. Student ID is harvested by calling each function with N=0 and null pointers.

nodes.label: rubric.h Ground Truth
nodes.rationale: Sets FLOATTYPE_COMPLEX64 so floatType is std::complex<float>, cuComplex on GPU, MKL_Complex8 as reference. rubric.h overrides any transcript on conflict.

nodes.label: ERR_TOLERANCE
nodes.rationale: 1e-7 summed |yours - ref|^2 over 4.2M elements is about 1.5e-7 RMS per element, only a few times above intrinsic float rounding noise for a K=2048 dot product, so summation order is part of correctness.

nodes.label: JudgementDay Graded Run
nodes.rationale: Pinned to the a100-a and a100-b node pair so comparisons run on identical hardware. First permitted use is Phase 7 with a budget of two runs; N=2048, 4 threads, 2 nodes, 15-minute wall.

nodes.label: Results Log Convention
nodes.rationale: Any number quoted in any doc must trace to a slurm-*.out.

nodes.label: Phase 0 Pipeline and Reconnaissance
nodes.rationale: Recalibrating every ratio estimate against the measured MKL reference is the highest-information ten minutes of the project.

nodes.label: Phase 1 CPU Correct Baseline
nodes.rationale: Manual float-pair arithmetic replaces std::complex operator* because that compiles to the catastrophically slow __mulsc3 libcall; i-k-j loop order streams B by rows.

nodes.label: Phase 4 GPU Correct Baseline
nodes.rationale: The naive one-thread-per-element kernel stays defined forever because the .cuh declares it; thread x maps to column for coalescing.

nodes.label: Phase 5 GPU Register Blocking and Transfer Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Whether the cuBLAS reference time includes transfers decides how much further pipeline work is worth doing.
nodes.norm_label: phase 5 gpu register blocking and transfer pipeline

nodes.label: Phase 6 MPI
nodes.rationale: The MPI ratio is dominated by CPU quality, so Phase 2 is a prerequisite. No MPI_Init or MPI_Finalize, the harness owns them; the N<=0 guard runs before any MPI call.

nodes.label: CPU Ladder
nodes.rationale: Rungs R0 to R5. The AVX1 no-FMA ceiling is 16 SP flops per cycle per core; the interleaved-AVX shuffle scheme stays a fallback only because it caps near 60 percent of peak by saturating the shuffle port.

nodes.label: GPU Ladder
nodes.rationale: Rungs G0 to G4. float4 loads are safe because harness buffers are 64-byte aligned; device-side caching of B keyed on pointer identity stays off by default because it risks correctness if the harness swaps buffers.

nodes.label: MPI Design
nodes.rationale: GPU-inside-MPI would crush the 0.6 line but the rubric words the MPI column as 2 nodes x 4 cores, so the default is CPU-only pending a spec check.

nodes.label: 4M Real GEMM Scheme
nodes.rationale: Computes complex C as four real GEMMs on planar data, 8N^3 real flops, avoiding the shuffle-port-bound interleaved-AVX alternative.

nodes.label: 3M Gauss Trick
nodes.rationale: Cuts work to about 6N^3 flops but spends error headroom; ship only if measured error stays at or below ERR_TOLERANCE/3, behind an args-selectable switch.

nodes.label: AVX1 16x4 Microkernel
nodes.rationale: Two ymm rows by four broadcast columns, eight ymm accumulators, _mm256_broadcast_ss for B, dual-issued _mm256_mul_ps and _mm256_add_ps because the grader flags give AVX1 with no FMA.

nodes.label: Planar Real Imaginary Split
nodes.rationale: Split done OpenMP-parallel so first-touch spreads pages across cores; scratch planes are static _mm_malloc 64-byte aligned allocated on first call.

nodes.label: Cache Blocking
nodes.rationale: Starting points Kc=256, Mc=96 with packed B panels; Kc/Mc/Nr wired to args[0..2] with graded-safe defaults.

nodes.label: MPI Row Split Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Rank p computes C rows [r0, r1) where rows(p) = N/P + (p < N%P), directly into &C[r0*N]; the row-range helper is defined non-static in matrixMultiply.cpp and forward-declared extern in matrixMultiplyMPI.cpp because both objects link into one binary.

nodes.label: MPI_Allgatherv Reassembly
nodes.rationale: Uses MPI_IN_PLACE with MPI_FLOAT and all counts doubled. Deliberate: MPI_COMPLEX is a Fortran type and MPI_C_FLOAT_COMPLEX is C99 _Complex, both occasionally misbehave in C++ builds, raw floats cannot break.

nodes.label: Open Uncertainties
nodes.rationale: Six unknowns each resolved by measurement rather than guessing, tied to the phase that measures them.

nodes.label: Assignment1_GradeBot
nodes.rationale: Has the main loop that runs all benchmarks and assigns the grade. Called as N, threads, runCPU, runGPU, runMPI, then arbitrary trailing integers that arrive in the args array for debugging or work splitting.

nodes.label: Judgement Day Slurm Script
nodes.rationale: Runs on a specific pinned node pair so everyone is compared on literally the same machines; not for daily use because everyone hitting the same two computers locks jobs up.

nodes.label: Debug Slurm Scripts
nodes.rationale: Almost identical to the judgement day script but run on whatever nodes are free, so they are the day-to-day debugging path.

nodes.label: Speed-Based Marking Table
nodes.rationale: 0 marks for no compile or no submission, 1 for compiles but wrong answer, 2 for works but very slow, higher marks by ratio against the reference library time.

nodes.label: Work Sharing For Loop
nodes.rationale: pragma omp for splits loop iterations across threads without duplication; only the outer loop of a nest is parallelised unless collapse is used.

nodes.label: Schedule Clause
nodes.rationale: Static apportions fixed chunks; dynamic lets threads pick up work as it becomes available, which can be faster because there is no guarantee threads progress at the same rate.

nodes.label: Collapse Clause
nodes.rationale: Joins nested loops into a single iteration space; only legal when the loops are independent of each other.

nodes.label: Data Sharing Clauses
nodes.rationale: private, firstprivate, lastprivate. Parallel regions do not necessarily initialise values, and default sharing varies by compiler, so uninitialised private copies are a portability trap.

nodes.label: Race Condition
nodes.rationale: Two threads load, add, and store the same variable; only one store survives, so results are sometimes right and sometimes wrong depending on timing.

nodes.label: OMP Critical
nodes.rationale: Catch-all one-thread-at-a-time section; inside a hot loop it can erase the entire parallel speedup.

nodes.label: OMP Atomic
nodes.rationale: Restricts exclusivity to a single read, write, or update rather than a whole block, so it can be faster than critical.

nodes.label: Per-Thread Partial Sums
nodes.rationale: Each thread accumulates privately at full speed and only the final merge is critical, so the serialised section runs once instead of once per iteration.

nodes.label: OMP Reduction
nodes.rationale: reduction(+:sum) replaces the parallel region, local sum, and critical merge with one clause, same speed with far less code.

nodes.label: OMP Sections
nodes.rationale: Parallelism without a for loop; threads beyond the number of sections sit idle unless nested regions give them work.

nodes.label: OMP Single and Master
nodes.rationale: single lets an arbitrary thread do a statement once; master pins it to thread zero.

nodes.label: OMP SIMD Directive
nodes.rationale: Tells the compiler a loop may be vectorised on top of threading; the speedup is compiler and environment dependent and not always reproducible.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo Sampling Example
nodes.rationale: Estimates pi by dart throwing and e by a running-sum trick; parallelising it is tricky because the RNG itself can become a hidden correctness bug.

nodes.label: Thread-Local Random Number Generator
nodes.rationale: Without thread_local, threads can initialise identical generators and produce the same random numbers, silently biasing the Monte Carlo estimate while still looking correct.

nodes.label: MPI Communicator
nodes.rationale: MPI_COMM_WORLD is the set of all tasks; it can be split into subgroups so collective operations apply only inside a group.

nodes.label: MPI Send and Receive
nodes.rationale: Point-to-point with buffer, count, datatype, destination or source, tag, and communicator; the receiver must post one receive per expected message.

nodes.label: MPI Reduce
nodes.rationale: Condenses a manual send-and-receive loop into one collective with an operation such as MPI_SUM delivered to a root task.

nodes.label: MPI Allreduce
nodes.rationale: Reduce combined with broadcast, so every task ends with the result and no root argument is needed.

nodes.label: MPI Scatter and Gather
nodes.rationale: Scatter splits a root buffer into equal segments across tasks; gather is the inverse and replaces a send-receive loop when no arithmetic combination is wanted.

nodes.label: MPI Alltoall
nodes.rationale: Every process sends to and receives from every other in one call, useful when no process should hold a master role.

nodes.label: Domain Decomposition with Remainder Handling
nodes.rationale: Each rank computes first and last indices from rank and world size; when N does not divide evenly the last rank picks up the slack, an unequal but simple fix. Splitting also divides memory since MPI memory is not shared.

nodes.label: Cluster Job Submission
nodes.rationale: module load then sbatch a script naming nodes and tasks; tasks on different nodes share no memory, which makes a multi-node run a true test that the MPI part works. Avoid running real jobs on the login node.

nodes.label: CUDA Kernel
nodes.rationale: Marked __global__, returns void, results go through an output pointer; a serial kernel on a GPU is far slower than the CPU because GPUs are built for parallel work.

nodes.label: CUDA Error Check Macro
nodes.rationale: do-while(false) wrapper checks every API return and prints cudaGetErrorString with __FILE__ and __LINE__ before aborting, so failures name their call site.

nodes.label: Parallel Reduction Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Halving tree with consecutive threads adding strided partners avoids warp divergence and bank conflicts. Reduction stays within a block because cross-block waiting can deadlock when the grid exceeds simultaneous capacity, so block results feed repeated kernel launches with ping-ponged buffers until one value remains.

nodes.label: __syncthreads Fence
nodes.rationale: Block-wide fence that must never sit behind a conditional some threads skip, or the block deadlocks.

nodes.label: Shared Memory
nodes.rationale: Per-block memory partitioned out of L1 cache, much faster than the global scratch buffer it replaces; dynamic extern __shared__ sized at launch, or static when the size is known at compile time.

nodes.label: Bank Conflicts
nodes.rationale: Shared memory has 32 banks; two threads of one warp touching different addresses in the same bank serialise. Consecutive-element access avoids this, and bank width can be set to 8 bytes for doubles.

nodes.label: Vectorized Memory Loads
nodes.rationale: Threads fetch efficiently up to 128 bits, so reinterpret_cast to double4 or float4 loads several elements per instruction; leftover elements need a tail switch and allocations must respect 256-bit alignment.

nodes.label: Global Thread Index
nodes.rationale: blockDim.x * blockIdx.x + threadIdx.x, with grid-stride loops so a launch smaller than N still covers every element.

nodes.label: Mark Harris Reduction PDF
nodes.author: Mark Harris
nodes.rationale: Nvidia presentation both tutors learned CUDA reduction from; partly outdated since Volta allowed intra-warp divergence, invalidating its implicit warp-synchronous last-warp unrolling.

nodes.label: Warp Shuffle Instructions
nodes.rationale: Warp-level primitives introduced because Volta threads within a warp can diverge, so warp-synchronous code needs explicit syncwarp or shuffle-based exchange.

nodes.label: Cooperative Groups
nodes.rationale: Nvidia's bundling of warp and block synchronisation primitives; can even synchronise a grid, collapsing the multi-launch reduction to a single kernel launch.

nodes.label: Default Stream Ordering
nodes.rationale: Kernel launches in the same stream execute in order, so the recursive reduction needs no explicit device synchronisation between steps.

nodes.label: COSC3500 Assignment: Parallel Programming Techniques
nodes.rationale: Implement three matrix multiply functions for three hardware configurations, benchmarked against gold standard reference implementations for N x N matrices, marks out of 21.

nodes.label: CPU Implementation (AVX/OpenMP)
nodes.rationale: Benchmarked on 4 cores against Intel MKL.

nodes.label: GPU Implementation (CUDA)
nodes.rationale: Benchmarked on 1 GPU against cuBLAS.

nodes.label: MPI Implementation (2 nodes, 4 cores each)
nodes.rationale: Runs on a cluster of two nodes against the MKL reference. It can reuse the CPU-based implementation from matrixMultiply.cpp.

nodes.label: Marking Rubric (Table 1)
nodes.rationale: Marks come from how many times longer the implementation's runtime is relative to the reference implementation (Intel MKL or cuBLAS), lower ratios are better. Marks are capped at 7 per implementation, 21 total.

nodes.label: Performance Ratio Thresholds
nodes.rationale: CPU (4 cores): 7 marks at 1.0x, 6 at 1.5x, 5 at 3.0x, 4 at 6.0x, 3 at 12.0x. GPU (1 GPU): 7 at 1.5x, 6 at 2.0x, 5 at 3.0x, 4 at 4.0x, 3 at 5.0x. MPI (2 nodes, 4 cores each): 7 at 0.6x, 6 at 1.0x, 5 at 1.5x, 4 at 3.0x, 3 at 6.0x. 2 marks if more than twice as slow as the 3-mark threshold without timing out, 1 if it compiles and runs but gives the wrong answer, 0 if it does not compile, was not submitted, or times out.

nodes.label: Intel MKL Reference Implementation
nodes.rationale: Gold standard reference for the CPU and MPI benchmarks.

nodes.label: cuBLAS Reference Implementation
nodes.rationale: Gold standard reference for the GPU benchmark.

nodes.label: Assignment1_GradeBot Benchmark Harness
nodes.rationale: Runs the benchmarks and assigns the marks out of 21. Usable from the command line for instant feedback before final grading.

nodes.label: GradeBot Command-Line Interface
nodes.rationale: ./Assignment1_GradeBot {matrix dimension} {threadCount} {runBenchmarkCPU} {runBenchmarkGPU} {runBenchmarkMPI} {optional integers...}. The optional integers are passed through to the matrixMultiply routines as the args array with argCount, for debugging and tweaking, and do not exist when the final JudgementDay script runs.

nodes.label: GradeBot Text Output Format
nodes.rationale: Writes to stdout and to per-benchmark per-node files COSC3500Assignment_{benchmark type}_{node}.txt with 6 columns: Info (implementation, thread/gpu/rank identifiers, hardware name), N (matrix dimension), Matrices/second (MKL reference), Matrices/second (your implementation), Error (sum of squares difference against the reference output), Grade (marks assigned).

nodes.label: Chained Unitary Matrix Benchmark
nodes.rationale: A set of random unitary square matrices is created and successively multiplied, A = A.B, each step multiplying the next matrix by the previous product. The final solution is checked against the reference to within an allowable floating point error while speed is measured relative to MKL or cuBLAS. For CPU and GPU the whole multiplication is on one machine in one memory space.

nodes.label: MPI Full-Copy Data Requirement
nodes.rationale: Each MPI node starts with its own identical copy of the full set of matrices, so no test data distribution is needed. Each node can compute its own portion of the multiply, but every node must end each step holding a full copy of the current matrix product, because the next multiplication needs the whole matrix.

nodes.label: ERR_TOLERANCE (rubric.h)
nodes.rationale: Allowed floating point error bound defined in rubric.h. Errors larger than this count as a failed implementation.

nodes.label: Three Editable Files Rule
nodes.rationale: Only matrixMultiply.cpp, matrixMultiplyGPU.cu, and matrixMultiplyMPI.cpp may be changed for the final submission. Unimplemented parts are submitted as the original blank default .cpp files. Any deviation from the format is rejected by the grading scripts.

nodes.label: No Outside Libraries Rule
nodes.rationale: Functions may not use any header files or outside libraries other than the provided headers matrixMultiply.h, matrixMultiplyGPU.cuh, and matrixMultiplyMPI.h.

nodes.label: No Stdout or File Writes Rule
nodes.rationale: The submitted functions must not write to stdout or to file in the final submission.
nodes.norm_label: no stdout or file writes rule

nodes.label: Provided Header Files
nodes.rationale: matrixMultiply.h, matrixMultiplyGPU.cuh, and matrixMultiplyMPI.h are the only headers the implementations may use.

nodes.label: Fixed matrixMultiply Function Signatures
nodes.rationale: The matrixMultiply routines take an args integer array and argCount parameter, filled from GradeBot's optional trailing CLI integers. Interpretation of the array is up to the student, and the array does not exist in the final grading run.

nodes.label: Final Submission Zip (48008361.zip)
nodes.rationale: One zip named 48008361.zip containing matrixMultiply.cpp, matrixMultiplyGPU.cu, matrixMultiplyMPI.cpp, and slurm.zip. The format must be followed strictly.

nodes.label: slurm.zip Job Output Archive
nodes.rationale: A zip archive containing all slurm job output files (slurm-xxxx.out) from the student's runs.

nodes.label: RangpurJudgementDay Grading Script
nodes.rationale: goslurm_COSC3500Assignment_RangpurJudgementDay is the slurm script used to assign the final grade. It runs on two nodes with the CPU and GPU benchmarks run once on each node, and the fastest node result is used. Students are asked not to submit all their jobs with it because it overwhelms the nodes.

nodes.label: Debug Slurm Scripts
nodes.rationale: Separate debug slurm scripts are provided for CPU, GPU, and MPI. Students should modify them to test only the section currently being worked on, instead of running the full JudgementDay script.

nodes.label: Rangpur Shared Assignment Directory
nodes.rationale: Assignment files live on rangpur at /home/groups/cosc3500/shared/matmul. Students copy the Makefile, the three matrixMultiply* files, and the /slurm/ submission scripts to their own directory to start.
